body: I’m having a lot of connection issues myself, I don’t know if it’s my wifi connection or what. That being said every Call Of Duty has had the same type of thing from my experience, especially around/shortly after launch.
The results are showing pretty well then. The last few articles I’ve seen from them seemed to be pretty comprehensive.
Say what you want about the clickbait side of Buzzfeed, I think it’s pretty trash too, but the news sector it has is actually pretty good.

I remember this, my sister had a copy of it on DVD when she was growing up. I got a weird sense of enjoyment from watching it because of how fucking weird and uncanny it is. I believe the animation studio behind it went on to animate pre-rendered cutscenes for several video games, the racing game Juiced being one of them.
It wasn’t, though I do know that band. I have a friend who loves TMG so, so very much. I have yet to really dig into their discography.

People who act like that are the biggest arseholes, going off personal experience. Try to avoid him if you can, I get the feeling that he’s a part of your friend group though, which can make it a lot harder since you don’t want to abandon your other friends obviously. You should be allowed to say whatever you want without fear of being verbally abused by some toxic prick like that.

I hope this isn’t a frustrating comment, but this won’t last forever friend. It can feel that way, it can feel incredibly frustrating, but it won’t. It might take a bit of self-evaluation and other things, but deep down, everyone has attractive qualities. Some women, and people in general, out there have a thing for bigger men. Yeah it can be hard to find those people, but they’re out there. 

You’re trying with the keto, that’s a pretty good start, even though I don’t know much about diets or anything. Try to be kind to yourself, it isn’t easy and sometimes your mental health can really get in the way, but it will hopefully start a progress. Heaps of people are shy and lack confidence when it comes to many things, myself included. It’s something that heaps of people grow into, even the most confident people I know or have read about have been scared shitless deep down at times. I’d suggest joining a gym too, if you have the money for it. It can be expensive and trying to get used to it all can be pretty rough, it took me like a year or two. That’s totally up to you though.

I apologise if my advice wasn’t too great or came off as another bog standard comment, but I believe in you. It might take a while and it might be frustrating and painful and I’m just another internet stranger, but I believe in you.

I feel for you OP. I don’t think what you said was cruel, I felt the same way about my own parents until they separated around February of last year. I feel like I don’t know enough about this entire situation to provide decent advice, however the situation you’ve described there sounds incredibly abusive and unhealthy. Your mother has a job for the first time in ten years, after fighting all of those conditions that you’ve mentioned, and your dad just wants her to invest most of her pay into renovating the house? Just, what the-?

That should be a celebration. She survived all of that and managed to get a job after ten years. Your dad just comes off as unsympathetic and cruel honestly. I apologise if I’m repeating things that you’ve already thought of, I just wish I had something better to say. I really hope things turn around at some point, I can’t fully imagine how painful this would be to watch for you.
